item.title: Megan Thee Stallion’s “Thin Ice” Streams Jump 152%
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion saw "Thin Ice" daily U.S. streams rise 152% after taking the Tina Tuesday freestyle beyond YouTube.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion saw daily U.S. on-demand streams for “Thin Ice” rise 152% between October 24 and 26.

According to Billboard’s report on Luminate data, the freestyle drew 98,000 streams Saturday, 174,000 Sunday and 247,000 Monday.

It reached streaming services October 24 after starting on YouTube. The three daily totals added up to about 519,000 streams over that stretch.

“Thin Ice” sampled the intro to Limp Bizkit’s “Break Stuff” and joined her Tina Tuesday freestyle series. The song had not entered the Hot 100 when Billboard reported the increase.

The official performance arrived on Megan’s YouTube channel on October 20 and ran two minutes and 27 seconds.

By October 28, the upload had more than 10.9 million views. That video counter covered a different period from the three days of streaming figures.

Megan told Marie Claire she had spent the summer recording and rewriting Act III after missing her intended summer release window.

Her new music also followed a change in the business behind her releases.

On August 14, Megan announced a partnership with Interscope Records that gave her access to its worldwide distribution and other support while she kept ownership of her masters and publishing.

Her company, Hot Girl Productions, remained home to her music.

She regained that control after a long fight with her former label.

As AllHipHop previously reported, she signed with Carl Crawford’s 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018 and sued the company in 2020. The two sides settled and separated in October 2023. They did not make the settlement terms public.

Hot Girl Productions had already released “Cobra” in November 2023 when Warner Music Group announced its agreement with Megan in February 2024.

Warner counted “HISS” as her second solo release through her own company. Radio promotion and marketing were among the services available under that deal. She kept control of her recordings, publishing and creative direction.

The agreement also let Megan use Warner’s network for other acts on her imprint.

“I’ve always wanted to create music on my terms while building a legacy that extends beyond the industry,” Megan said in her Interscope announcement.

item.title: Outkast’s Nike Collection Heads To More Stores
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Outkast joined Nike, Class Trip and the University of Georgia for a clothing collection with a wider retail rollout set for October 28.
item.content:encoded:
Outkast teamed with Nike, Class Trip and the University of Georgia to create clothes inspired by the duo’s style, with a wider rollout that started on October 28.

Nike plans to bring the full Outkast U range to nike.com and select stores, following the October 27 launch through SNKRS, Class Trip and Atlanta retailers.

The clothes borrow from André 3000 and Big Boi’s wardrobes. Georgia’s G carries Outkast’s crown, while jerseys bear 96, a nod to the year ATLiens arrived. The duo’s “Roses” video also helped guide the look.

Class Trip founder Brian Francis said André’s recollections of visiting Athens came up over lunch, which gave the project its start.

A red varsity jacket pairs wool with black leather sleeves. It uses chenille patches and chain-stitch embroidery, with Georgia and Outkast lettering across the back. The range also includes rugby shirts, a satin bomber and tees.

“We wanted to create something as timeless as their music,” said Jon Tietz, Class Trip’s creative director.

Class Trip’s store listed the crown snapback at $50 and the “Ms. Jackson” T-shirt at $60. The cotton jersey was $145, and the hoodie was $180.

The partnership follows Outkast’s Waffle House collaboration, which launched through the group’s website on October 2.

That project took a line from Big Boi’s “So Fresh, So Clean” verse and turned it into a Waffle House marquee, connecting the duo’s catalog with another familiar piece of Southern life.

Hip-Hop historian NuFace discussed that earlier pairing in an interview with AllHipHop.

“OutKast has become part of the culture, the identity and the language of Atlanta,” he told AllHipHop about the Waffle House collaboration. No new OutKast music was announced with that partnership.

The connection has roots in the music: André and Big Boi released their debut, Southernplayalisticadillacmuzik, in 1994, then built on it with ATLiens, Aquemini and Stankonia.

Their reach also earned them a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s 2025 class, with Donald Glover serving as their inductor.

The Hall’s profile traces a sound that drew on funk and jazz as well as rap, part of the range behind that recognition. The Hall counts Outkast among the few Hip-Hop acts to win the Grammy for Album of the Year.

item.title: R. Kelly Finds The Wildest Supporter Who Says Black Community Failed Him
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Iyanla Vanzant sought forgiveness during a wildly candid exchange that said mentorship failed the incarcerated R&B singer.
item.content:encoded:
Iyanla Vanzant Apologized To R. Kelly And Said Community Elders Failed Him

Iyanla Vanzant apologized to R. Kelly on “The Jason Lee Show” over what she described as the Black community’s failure to support him before his imprisonment for sexual abuse.

The author and television personality directed her apology toward the singer while discussing the responsibilities of community elders. Her remarks focused on missed opportunities to address his personal struggles and the people who benefited financially from his career, according to Baller Alert’s account of the interview.

“Forgive me as an elder in our community not being available to support you,” Vanzant said. “Forgive me for ignoring your pain. Forgive me for abandoning you.” 

When host Jason Lee questioned whether she believed she had personally abandoned Kelly, Vanzant expanded her answer to include the broader community.

“Our entire community abandoned him. As an elder, I’m going to own it,” she said.

Vanzant also questioned why people who earned money through Kelly’s success had not done more to help with his reading difficulties. She presented those circumstances as examples of support she believed should have accompanied his commercial achievements. Those assertions represent her assessment of the people surrounding Kelly, rather than findings about what caused his criminal conduct. 

The interview appeared in an Oct. 21 post from Hollywood Unlocked, which described a broader conversation about forgiveness, grief, personal responsibility and celebrity culture. Kelly was among several public figures discussed during the episode.

Her apology comes with a substantial criminal record as its backdrop.

A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Kelly in September 2021 of racketeering and other offenses involving the exploitation of women and children. U.S. District Judge Ann M. Donnelly sentenced him to 30 years in prison in June 2022. Prosecutors said his operation depended on associates who helped facilitate the abuse. 

A separate Chicago jury convicted Kelly in September 2022 of three counts of producing child sexual abuse material and three counts of enticing a minor into sexual activity. He received a 20-year sentence in February 2023, with one year ordered to run consecutively to his New York sentence, producing a combined 31-year term. 

Vanzant’s argument places attention on opportunities she believes were missed before those prosecutions.

The court record establishes another responsibility: Kelly’s own actions toward the women and children he abused. Her appeal for compassion adds to that public conversation without changing the crimes established at trial.

item.title: Drake Earns Third Latin Airplay No. 1
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Drake's "Ahí" collaboration with Karol G topped Latin Airplay, extending an October filled with chart milestones and RIAA honors.
item.content:encoded:
Drake kept his chart run going as “Ahí” with Karol G reached No. 1 on Latin Airplay.

The song rose from No. 2 on the October 31 chart with a 5% gain in Latin radio audience during October 16–22, according to Billboard.

It marked his third No. 1 there, after Romeo Santos’ “Odio” in 2014 and Bad Bunny’s “MIA” in 2018. Karol G earned her 23rd leader, passing Prince Royce.

The duet also topped Latin Rhythm Airplay. On Hot Latin Songs, it stood at No. 3 after a one-week stay at No. 1. It was No. 88 on the Hot 100, where it had peaked at No. 44.

The track appeared on Karol G’s August album No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto, released through Bichota/Interscope Capitol.

Drake’s own new releases had already posted big gains on the album and singles charts earlier in October. HABIBTI became his 18th No. 1 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. That put him ahead of Future and the Temptations, who each had 17.

The jump followed the HABIBTI (FOMO) expansion, which added four songs from his “FOMO” film. For the October 17 chart, the album rose from No. 35 and replaced his own ICEMAN at the top. It also returned to No. 2 on the Billboard 200 after sitting at No. 116. The project earned 71,000 U.S. album-equivalent units for the week ending October 8, a 506% increase.

Streaming accounted for nearly 70,000 of those units.

That same expansion included “Solar Eclipse,” his duet with Don Toliver. The song entered the Hot 100 at No. 5, bringing Drake’s record tally of top 10 hits to 91.

It also gave him his 33rd No. 1 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs. The track drew 15.1 million U.S. streams in its first week.

There was fresh recognition for his older work as well. AllHipHop reported that Views went diamond as an October 23 RIAA update brought new awards across his catalog.

The RIAA’s diamond level represents 10 million units, including eligible sales and streams in the United States.

The same update put Scorpion at nine times platinum, More Life at six times and Certified Lover Boy at five times.

It also listed So Far Gone at three times platinum and Care Package at platinum.

item.title: Whoopi Goldberg Says A Good Check Keeps Her On “The View”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Whoopi Goldberg explained why her "The View" paycheck kept her coming back and compared her TV job with Hollywood movie pay.
item.content:encoded:
Whoopi Goldberg gave a three-word answer when asked why she keeps returning to “The View” after nearly two decades: “A good check.”

In a W interview, she compared her TV pay with what Hollywood would offer her.

“That’s really what it is. I’m well-paid, and I do a good job. I earn my dough, and sometimes people like it, sometimes they don’t. No one is going to pay me guy money to be in a movie. I get what I can, have as good a time as I can, and I don’t really worry about it too much,” Goldberg reasoned.

She said Bette Midler had been the first choice for “Sister Act,” a role Goldberg got after Midler passed on it.

Goldberg said she earned her salary. She also said Barbara Walters hired her to share her opinions, something she still took seriously.

The paycheck was already a topic when she visited Keke Palmer’s “Baby, This Is Keke Palmer” podcast on August 4.

According to TheWrap, Goldberg told Palmer the amount would surprise people, though she did not reveal a dollar figure. She also explained that she needed work, which brought her to the daytime panel.

“I needed a job. Barbara [Walters] offered me a job,” she said. Goldberg had been working in radio when Walters approached her about an opening on the show. She accepted the offer.

In that August conversation, Goldberg said she appreciated having reliable work while others struggled to find jobs.

She also said she enjoyed the chance to talk through issues and exchange ideas with people. Viewers who disagreed with her didn’t change that: different opinions were part of the job.

The first “Sister Act” arrived in 1992. Goldberg returned for “Sister Act 2: Back in the Habit” the following year, with Lauryn Hill among the cast. A third movie would bring Goldberg back to a series whose first two installments came out more than three decades ago.

Her plans for another “Sister Act” have included some familiar names in music. In her 2022 conversation with Charlamagne Tha God, Goldberg said she wanted Nicki Minaj, Lizzo and Palmer to join her in the third film. She was discussing a wish list at the time, with a script expected later that month.

The W conversation also returned to “Sister Act 3.” Goldberg said she had hoped to make it before Maggie Smith died. Fans around the world still embraced the films, she said.

item.title: Drake’s Birthday Bracelet Honors Adonis & Iceman
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drake received a custom diamond bracelet for his 40th birthday, with Adonis on one side and his album Iceman on the other.
item.content:encoded:
Drake received a diamond birthday bracelet honoring his son and his music: one side spelled out Adonis, while the other carried his album name, Iceman.

The rapper turned 40 on October 24. Alessandro Bernini of Bernini High Jewelry and designer Domenico Formichetti created the custom piece, according to Page Six. Bernini described the materials as white gold, natural gemstones and F-color diamonds with VS clarity.

The bracelet was handmade in Italy and featured several shades of blue. Its letter charms honored Drake’s 9-year-old son, Adonis Graham, alongside the album. Experts estimated the bracelet at more than 20 carats.

The design also gave Drake something to wear alongside his custom Ice Gradient Daytona Rolex. He showed off that watch in August, months before his birthday.

Jewelry trade publication JCK described the Rolex’s band as a progression from baguette-cut diamonds into blue sapphires. Sapphires also lined its bezel, while diamonds covered parts of the factory-made watch in a pavé setting.

The watch connected to Iceman in ways beyond its colors. An engraving on the back read “Freeze the world,” a line from the album’s song “Make Them Know.”

Drake presented the watch on Instagram to celebrate his achievements in 2026.

That pair joined another piece of jewelry with a personal reference. Drake’s Alex Moss necklace took its shape from Cogsworth, the clock character in “Beauty and the Beast.” The necklace held nearly 155 carats of white diamonds and paid tribute to the late fashion designer Virgil Abloh.

Drake also held a birthday celebration in New York City on October 23, a day before he turned 40.

More than 400 friends and family members attended, and the Backstreet Boys performed. Guests could leave with Chanel and Hermès handbags or cash prizes worth up to $1 million.

Drake also held a second celebration on October 24. Travis Scott and Jack Harlow were among the guests for the party on his actual birthday.

item.title: Macklemore Brings Dead Prez & Kneecap To Dublin Benefit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Macklemore brought Hozier and Kneecap to his Dublin benefit, where songs and appeals for Palestinians shared the stage.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore brought Hozier and Kneecap to Dublin’s 3Arena, as his “Free Palestine” concert series began with guest performances and appeals for aid.

The sold-out show drew up to 13,000 people, according to the BBC. Fans traveled from Belfast and Cork for the concert. Macklemore pledged the tour’s proceeds to organizations supporting Palestinians.

The Journal reported that actor Liam Cunningham welcomed the crowd before Palestinian singer Lina Makoul began the music.

DJ Habibeats, Dead Prez and Irish folk band Beoga also performed. A Gaza Children’s Choir performance appeared by video during the evening. Kneecap opened with “H.O.O.D.” as fans formed a mosh pit.

The beneficiaries included Gaza Soup Kitchen, Medical Aid for Palestinians and the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund.

Hozier performed “Too Sweet” and asked the Irish government to approve visas for 55 students in Gaza. He said the students had earned scholarship places in Ireland and directed fans toward a petition on the screen behind him.

Macklemore looked back at his exit from Sheeran’s tour. He thanked Hozier and Kneecap for saying yes when he called. “And how fitting that the first show would be in Ireland,” he said.

The tour followed his removal from Ed Sheeran’s U.S. dates after pro-Palestinian speeches at MetLife Stadium in September.

Sheeran said the tour organizers made the decision and later apologized for how he handled the dispute. Patriots owner Robert Kraft objected to the rapper’s appearance at Gillette Stadium, citing rhetoric and imagery he considered offensive to Jewish people.

Macklemore rejected that characterization, distinguishing criticism of Israel from hostility toward Jewish people and calling for equal treatment.

As AllHipHop previously reported, he had already returned to the stage at Colorado’s Red Rocks on October 22, where he also spoke against ICE.

Macklemore took the stage after 10 P.M., used water guns during “White Walls” and later changed into a Bohemians jersey.

His songs included “Same Love” and “Hind’s Hall.” For the encore, he sang a song he said he wrote a week earlier, then closed with “Can’t Hold Us.”

The benefit series continues in Paris on Thursday, October 29, then moves to London on Friday, October 30.

item.title: AI Vocal Worker Suing Kanye Fears For His Safety, Asks To Remain Anonymous
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kanye West's accuser awaited a ruling on anonymity in a lawsuit seeking payment for AI vocal work on "Vultures 2" and "Bully."
item.content:encoded:
A producer suing Kanye West for at least $220,000 over allegedly unpaid AI vocal work faced a delay in his bid to keep his name private.

Judge Kristin S. Escalante heard arguments in Los Angeles Superior Court, then continued the hearing.

The producer, suing as John Doe, named Ye and Yeezy Record Label LLC as defendants on August 3. He alleged he had not been paid, given a written contract or credited on streaming platforms.

His attorney, Mark Steven Avila, cited fears for Doe’s safety and his family’s safety in court papers reported by MyNewsLA. The request would shield his legal name, home address and relatives’ identifying details without sealing the complaint or closing proceedings.

“Every allegation, every filing and every ruling in this case remains fully public,” Avila wrote, according to MyNewsLA.

The complaint reported that Doe sought at least $110,000 for seven released tracks, plus double damages under Los Angeles’ freelance worker ordinance. The complaint alleged that Ye and Yeezy recognized his contributions, promised changes to streaming credits and later offered a master buyout.

Doe said he was hired on August 1, 2024, two days before Vultures 2 arrived. He said he recorded his own voice as source material and made more than 400 vocal generations using at least 13 custom AI voice models.

He claimed contributions to five tracks on the album.

He said work on Bully began in October 2024 and included more AI vocal production, along with writing contributions to two released songs.

Los Angeles’ ordinance requires written agreements for covered freelance contracts worth at least $600, including when jobs for the same client reach that amount within a calendar year.

The agreement must spell out the services, compensation and payment deadline. The ordinance also allows damages of up to twice the unpaid amount if payment is late.

A separate case involving Ye’s former intelligence aide raised a similar privacy issue in 2025. A judge allowed that different plaintiff to use a pseudonym, finding that keeping his name private would not hinder discovery or depositions.

For the producer, the next hearing on anonymity is set for November 18.

item.title: Da’Vinchi Offered An Apology. Is It Enough?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Da’Vinchi apologized for his silly wording and challenged how his comments about Americans and slavery were taken.
item.content:encoded:
Da’Vinchi has offered an apology, and since we gave him a well deserved roasting, fairness requires giving his response some room, too. We cannot have unlimited space for the criticism and suddenly run out of ink when somebody addresses it.

The actor appeared on “The Breakfast Club” October 27 to revisit the comments he made during Cam Newton’s “Funky Friday” podcast. That conversation about American work ethic, parenting and overseas actors getting American roles earned him considerably more attention than a routine promotional interview. 

“I apologize that my wording was harsh,” Da’Vinchi said. He acknowledged that his language muddled the point he intended to make and said he understood why people were offended.

Good. Because calling people incompetent is generally a poor opening for a productive discussion. Somewhere between making an observation and delivering a national performance review, the conversation went sideways.

READ ALSO: BMF Actor Da’Vinchi Angers Black Americans Over “Lazy Comment …”

During the original interview, Da’Vinchi said:

“I do think that the work ethic of Americans is one that people in a higher position don’t feel they can trust them.”

That is a sweeping assessment. Add a discussion about Black actors from abroad landing American roles, and it should surprise absolutely nobody that Black Americans took exception.

Still, accuracy matters here. Da’Vinchi disputed the claim that he called Black people lazy, explaining that his criticism concerned Americans broadly. He also denied telling people to forget slavery. Asked whether slavery was an excuse for present circumstances, he answered, “It’s not an excuse. It’s a reality. It’s why we’re here right now.”

That clarification deserves to appear alongside the original controversy. Whether it satisfies everybody is another question entirely.

My issue with these discussions is how quickly personal upbringing becomes a measuring stick for millions of strangers. Being raised in a strict household can teach independence. It does not automatically qualify anyone to diagnose an entire population.

But an apology should have somewhere to land. People can hear him out without pretending the original remarks were harmless. They can also remain unconvinced without demanding a lifetime sentence in the comments.

We can note this got less than 100k views and well under 2,000 comments. Might be too little too late.

item.title: Project Pat Takes “Chickenhead” To Church’s
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Project Pat joined Lil Lucky for Church's Texas Chicken's "Chickahhhn," turning a viral remake into a branded collaboration.
item.content:encoded:
Project Pat took “Chickenhead” into a restaurant campaign, teaming up with Lil Lucky for Church’s Texas Chicken’s “Chickahhhn.”

According to the company’s announcement, the collaboration grew from Lil Lucky’s viral Church’s remake. Creative agency Brunner saw the clip, pitched Church’s and helped bring the two artists together. The song and video premiered on the chain’s YouTube channel.

The brand went with old cars and its vintage logo for the visuals. Its announcement disclosed no financial terms.

“At Church’s, bringing people together is an important part of our DNA, and that goes beyond the food we serve. We’re committed to showing up for our local communities and creating experiences that bring people together,” said Roland Gonzalez, CEO of Church’s Texas Chicken. “Music is a powerful way to connect with people and celebrate the culture that makes our communities special. Partnering with Project Pat on ‘Chickahhhn’ helps us take the connection to another level.”

The chain had also brought Juvenile and Mannie Fresh into a Chicago restaurant to serve lunch alongside employees, making Pat’s collaboration part of a wider push involving Hip-Hop artists.

“Chickenhead” had already found new audiences well beyond its original run. The Memphis hit dated to 2001, with La Chat trading lines with Pat.

Cardi B reworked the song as “Bickenhead” on her 2018 debut, Invasion of Privacy. Another revival came through Alaynna Doty, a separate viral performer.

As AllHipHop previously reported, the 9-year-old from Olive Branch, Mississippi, performed “Chickenhead” at the Crazy Cactus restaurant in July 2025. Her mother, Lauren Durham, posted the clip to TikTok, and Pat later shared it himself.

By that July report, the clip had passed 4 million views and drawn more than 130,000 comments.

That summer, Pat invited Doty to join him for a planned September 1 performance on Beale Street’s main stage at Memphis’ 901 Day celebration. Gus’ World-Famous Fried Chicken in Nashville helped arrange the connection.
